label: input token v in the original phase, early positions (t<=5)
explanation: Token detector for v being read during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. It fires only when the input is v, essentially never on other tokens, at the delimiter, or during copy (129 tiny copy-phase activations, about 0% of mass, when v is fed back). It is restricted to early positions: rate is flat for t=0..4, falls at t=5 (many false positives there), and is zero for t>=6. Magnitude is highest at t=0..2 (top examples are v at t=1, after i) and falls off at later positions; v at t=4-5 activates weakly. Repeated occurrences of v also activate more weakly (in_first=0 holds 5% of mass).

issues: Only gap: at t=5 the feature fires on v about 60% of the time (dev precision about 0.60 at every L from 6 to 9, so length doesn't explain it). This produces most of the 4550 test false positives. It looks like a firing-threshold effect from activation fading with position. Firing is somewhat more likely when the v is a repeat (in_first==0 precision 0.81 vs 0.56) and when no digits have appeared yet (n_digits==0 0.67 vs 0.50 when n_digits>=2). Neither gives a clean rule, and t=5 holds only about 0.6% of activation mass.

Dropping t=5 (predicate t<=4) gives precision 1.0, but dev recall falls to 0.92 and F1 to 0.96, so the original predicate is the better trade-off. Restricting t=5 by length (L<=7) scores worse on test (F1 0.967 vs 0.974).
Test misses (133 steps, about 0% of mass) are all faint firings when v is fed back in the copy phase. This matches the claim of 129 weak copy-phase firings on dev.

The other claims check out on the dev profile. The feature fires only on in_tok v, never at <DEL>. Firing rate is flat at about 0.033 for original positions 0 to 4, drops to 0.020 at position 5, and is 0 from position 6 on. Activation mass is concentrated at t=0..2. in_first=0 carries 5.4% of mass, and the top examples are v at t=1 after i.
